page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.se1 family, running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include any local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the processor performance is generally modest. Single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, alongside Geekbench scores, place the instance in the bottom 25% of tested hardware. Similarly, single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression show poor performance, falling into the bottom 10%. However, the instance demonstrates average capabilities in large-block memory bandwidth read and write tests, as well as Passmark CPU physics and extended instruction tests. Redis SET operations and LLM inference for small 135M models also perform at an average level, though larger 7B model inference drops to the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.se1.2xlarge offers a high memory-to-core ratio, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high-frequency compute power. The lack of local storage means workloads must rely on external network-attached storage. This server is best suited for memory-optimized tasks such as caching layers, Redis deployments, small-scale database operations, and general-purpose workloads requiring a larger memory footprint than standard compute instances.
